item.title: Harvey County Sheriff’s Office seeks more female deputies to maintain safety, compliance at detention center
item.description: With female deputies absent from 30 detention center shifts last month, the Harvey County Sheriff’s Office says it urgently needs more women on staff — a move that would help protect female inmates and keep the jail in compliance with federal safety standards.

item.title: Letters to the editor: Lost in profanity
item.description: As long as there are two individuals in this world there will be the probability of a difference of opinion on some issue. item.title: In arresting and prosecuting journalists, Trump administration draws from authoritarian playbook
item.description: Like many Americans, I am deeply concerned about the Trump regime’s unhinged and unchecked authoritarian tactics. U.S. Immigration and Enforcement agents killing peaceful protestors on the street. Officials threatening lawyers and universities. Now, the administration is going after journalists who report the news.

item.title: Early voting to begin Feb. 17 for USD 373 bond election
item.description: Early voting for the Newton USD 373 bond election will begin Feb. 17 at the Harvey County Courthouse, 800 N. Main.

item.title: Is $8.3 million justice in the death of Kansas teenager? Can repeat cases be prevented?
item.description: A Sedgwick County federal court jury recently awarded C.J. Lofton’s family $8.3 million in compensation for Lofton’s death at the hands of juvenile intake officers. They held Lofton facedown for more than 30 minutes, killing him.

item.title: Sheriff: Current jail rates no longer cover costs
item.description: Sheriff Chad Gay is opening up a conversation with the Harvey County Commission about how much the county is charging outside agencies to house inmates at the Harvey County Detention Center.

item.title: County tables tax exemption approval for more discussion of process
item.description: Two items on the Harvey County Commission agenda were tabled Feb. 17, each with the extension of tax exemptions for local businesses.

item.title: Free pet microchip scanner helps reunite lost animals in Newton
item.description: It’s unassuming, looks just like an out-of-place light post in the front yard of a house on East 12th Street. But looks are deceiving when considering a new free service by Blue Skies Pet Care.
